Resolves #18359

Both projection catch blocks annotated the caught value unconditionally. `Neo.isDestroyed` is `Symbol.for('Neo.isDestroyed')` and the engine rejects pending awaits with it on destroy — including the `host.promiseUpdate()` awaited inside those try blocks — so a destroy-time rejection threw a `TypeError` on the annotation, the recovery never ran, and the sentinel was replaced by an error naming none of the cause. Both sites now rethrow it untouched.

Evidence: L3 (unit arms drive the real projection transaction in-process and observe the recovery seam directly) → L3 required (every AC on #18359 is a unit-observable property of the catch block). Residual: none.

Micro-review eligible: single-mechanism defect — two guard lines against an idiom already used ten times in-tree, with a four-arm red-first witness.

## AC Evidence
| AC-1 | CI-covered: `DockProjectionDestroySentinel.spec.mjs` — "the FIRST projection rethrows the destroy sentinel untouched" and "a staged projection rethrows the destroy sentinel untouched"; both RED before the fix with the exact `TypeError`, green after |
| AC-2 | CI-covered: the two `settleFailed*Calls` counters assert `0` on the sentinel path in those arms, and `1` on the ordinary-`Error` arms in the same fixture — the pair is what separates "guarded" from "recovery stopped running" |
| AC-3 | CI-covered: one sentinel arm per catch site — `Reconciler.mjs:465` reached via the public `onProjectionStaged` seam on the first projection, `:560` via a staged restructure |
| AC-4 | CI-covered: both ordinary-`Error` arms assert `isDockProjectionFailure === true`, the recovery ran, and `projectionRecovery` is one of the four published verdict strings |
| AC-5 | dashboard unit 837/837 locally at head; `components/dashboard` runs in CI. No pre-existing intermittent was absorbed — this branch touches neither of the two arms `#18215` and `#18290` track |

## Deltas from ticket
None substantive. The ticket prescribed the guard shape (`=== Neo.isDestroyed`, both sites, sentinel rethrown rather than recovered) and that is what shipped.

One implementation note the ticket left open: at `:465` the guard folds into the existing `if (!initialProjection) throw error` as a second disjunct rather than adding a branch, because both conditions mean the same thing there — this catch does not own the failure.

## Test Evidence
All coverage runs in CI.

The one thing a green suite cannot show is the red-first ordering, so it is recorded here: before the `src/` change the two sentinel arms failed with `Received: [TypeError: Cannot create property 'isDockProjectionFailure' on symbol 'Symbol(Neo.isDestroyed)']` while both ordinary-`Error` arms already passed. The controls were green throughout, which is what makes the post-fix green mean "the sentinel is guarded" rather than "the recovery stopped running".

## Post-Merge Validation
Nothing is owed after merge. Every AC is observable in-process; no item here depends on a deployed surface, a live service, or a later run.

## Evolution
Found while probing #18352, and only after two of my own probes were wrong. The first unregistered components from `Neo.manager.Instance`; `util.VDom.getVdom` resolves through `Neo.manager.Component`, a separate singleton, so nothing the vdom layer reads was ever removed and no flight rejected — I had published "the poison target is wrong" on that basis and withdrew it. Correcting the registry produced a real rejection, which surfaced this defect. The boundary stated on #18359 holds here: the route to the sentinel was constructed, there is no production sighting, and none is claimed — the defect is provable from the catch's assumption, the engine's documented sentinel, and the ten existing guards without one.
